title: Franchise E-Contracts: Sign Agreements 80% Faster with FDAM
description: Paper franchise agreements are slow, risky and hard to renew. See how FDAM e-contracts automate drafting, signing and renewal to close deals up to 80% faster.
html:
An introduction to FDAM's e-contract feature, which makes signing franchise agreements up to 80% faster

franchise ERP, e-contracts, franchise e-agreements, franchise operations, franchise store management, franchise systems, franchise agreements, contract management, franchise software, FDAM

Key takeaways

· Paper contracts come with three built-in limitations: signing delays, the risk of loss or forgery, and difficult renewal management.

· Moving to e-contracts makes signing franchise agreements 80% faster while reducing the risk of loss and forgery.

· FDAM's e-contract feature automates the entire process from drafting and signing to renewal, and alerts you 30 days before expiry so nothing slips through.

· Blockchain-based storage makes tampering impossible, and the feature meets the requirements of both Korea's Digital Signature Act and Franchise Business Act.

Franchise e-contractsare a way for headquarters to sign and manage the entire contracting process with franchise stores in a digital environment. With no paper to mail and no manual filing, HQ can send agreements by email, text or KakaoTalk and get them signed instantly on mobile, taking headquarters operations up a level.

Franchisor headquarters deal with many kinds of contracts every day, including franchise agreements, operating agreements and supply agreements. FDAM, built by MS Venter after nearly 25 years focused on franchise IT, is designed to standardize these HQ contract workflows inside an ERP. In this post, we walk through the limits of paper contracts, the value of e-contracts, and FDAM's e-contract feature, in that order.

Leave paper behind and handle franchise agreements digitally.

1. Three limitations of traditional franchise contracting

As long as headquarters sticks with paper contracts, the burden of contract management climbs steeply as the number of stores grows. Here are the three limitations HQ teams run into most often.

1) Signing delays

· HQ drafts and prints the agreement, then mails it to the store owner

· The store owner reviews and signs it, then mails it back to HQ

· Final review and confirmation take at least 1 to 2 weeks

Solution — With e-contracts, agreements can be signed instantly on mobile and PC.

2) Legal risk (loss and forgery)

· If the original is lost, proving legal validity becomes difficult

· Contract terms can potentially be altered after the fact

Solution — E-contracts are stored on a blockchain basis, blocking forgery at the source.

3) Inefficient contract management

· Paper storage makes searching and viewing cumbersome

· Renewal schedules are tracked manually in tools like Excel

Solution — Agreements and renewal schedules can be managed together, automatically, inside the franchise ERP.

2. Three ways e-contracts change franchise contracting

1) Sign online, instantly

· Send agreements to store owners by email, text or KakaoTalk

· Store owners e-sign right away on mobile or PC

· HQ tracks and approves contract status in real time on the same screen

In one real-world case, a franchisor headquarters cut its average contract signing time by more than 5xcompared with paper contracts.

2) Stronger legal validity and security

· Compliance with the Digital Signature Act and the Korea Fair Trade Commission's Franchise Business Act

· Contract history (signing time, IP, change log) stored in the system

· Blockchain-based encryption to block forgery

How HQ normally runs its contracting process accumulates in the system as-is, so HQ's supporting records are not scattered if a dispute arises.

3) Contract automation built on ERP integration

The franchise ERP FDAM has e-contracts built in, so the entire process from drafting to renewal is automated within one system.

· Real-time contract status (pending, signed, on hold, etc.)

· Automatic renewal alerts (sent 30 days before expiry)

· Central contract repository (instant search and download when needed)

Example of the contract management screen in FDAM ERP.

3. Three benefits HQ gains from FDAM e-contracts

Headquarters has to sign and manage contracts with many franchise stores. Drawing on experience working with about 500 brands, FDAM's module design reflects how HQ contract workflows actually run, so the system settles into the way headquarters already works.

1) Fast, accurate signing with digital franchise agreements

· Prospective store owners review and sign agreements instantly via email or text

· Signed agreements are saved automatically in the ERP, with no separate document handling

2) Real-time monitoring of contract progress

· HQ sees requested, in-progress and completed contracts on one screen

· Each store's contract history is saved automatically in the ERP database

3) Expiry and renewal management

· Review each store's renewal and term-by-term contract list to prevent missed renewals

· Automatic alerts 30 days before expiry give HQ time to respond

· New contract requests can also be handled in the ERP system

Ask the AI assistant, the first to be built into a Korean franchise ERP, "Which stores expire this month?" and you get the answer back instantly, organized as a table.

4. Franchise e-contracts are now a must, not an option

Put simply, the contract-related burdens headquarters face come down to three questions.

Three questions HQ faces

① Want to cut franchise agreement signing time by 80% or more?

② Want to completely eliminate the risk of lost or forged contracts?

③ Want to boost HQ operational efficiency by automating contract management?

All three questions lead to the same answer: FDAM's e-contract feature can solve them.

Frequently asked questions

Q. Do e-contracts have the same legal force as paper contracts?

E-contracts that meet the requirements of the Digital Signature Act and the Franchise Business Act have the same legal force as paper contracts. With FDAM e-contracts, contract history such as signing time, IP and change log is stored in the system, so HQ can use it as supporting evidence if a dispute arises.

Q. What does blockchain-based storage actually do?

The biggest benefit of blockchain-based storage is that contract content is encrypted in distributed form, making after-the-fact tampering practically impossible. Because the way HQ normally runs its contracting stays on record without alteration, confidence in HQ operations rises along with it.

Q. When are contract renewal alerts sent?

FDAM sends automatic alerts 30 days before a contract expires, so HQ has enough time to handle renewals. You can also view each store's renewal and term-by-term contract list, keeping HQ operations stable with no missed renewals.

Q. Can we move our existing paper contract history into the system?

Existing paper agreements can be digitized and registered in the system during initial setup. During the sales consultation, we review the format of the records your headquarters holds and recommend the most suitable migration approach.
